title: A matrix capacitance correction reduced low-frequency transfer error in passive models of two partial adult worm electrical maps
abstract: We tested frequency transfer after removal of 170 neurons from passive electrical models of two partial adult worm maps. Ten named locomotion interneurons were retained. Unit leak and capacitance and count-weighted symmetric conductance were assumed. At the primary coupling scale and dimensionless angular frequency 0.1, a matrix capacitance correction reduced relative transfer error from 0.6215% to 0.0322% in adult 7 and from 0.5393% to 0.0295% in adult 8. A diagonal correction left errors of 0.2989% and 0.2390%. The matrix correction matched the first frequency derivative, but did not give a uniformly wider 5% error range than the diagonal correction. It became less accurate than original capacitance at high frequency. Full-system and independent spectral checks agreed. This is a reproducible model benchmark, not a measured activity result. Partial electrical annotation, assumed cell parameters, one retained set, and two maps limit biological interpretation.

display.caption: Transfer error for ten retained cells in each partial adult worm map at the primary coupling scale. The matrix correction improves low-frequency accuracy and loses accuracy at high frequency. The dashed line is 5% error.
